title: Kuafu Chases the Sun

source.book: Classic of Mountains and Seas, Northern Lands Beyond the Sea
source.quote: Kuafu raced the sun. Thirsty, he drank the Yellow River and the Wei, and when those were not enough he set off for the great marsh, but died of thirst on the way. His staff, cast aside, became a grove of peach trees.

moral: He never caught the sun, but his staff grew into a grove of peach trees.

story.title: The Giant Kuafu
story.text: A giant named Kuafu decided to catch the sun.
story.narration: Long ago there was a giant called Kuafu. He watched the sun rise and set, and said: I will catch it.

story.title: On and On
story.text: He ran over mountains and rivers, all the way to where the sun goes down.
story.narration: Kuafu strode on, over mountain after mountain and river after river. When he was thirsty he drank the Yellow River and the Wei dry, and ran on.

keyMoment.question: The sun runs so fast — should he keep chasing?

options.text: He can't catch it, so sit down and rest
He can't catch it, and chases it anyway

keyMoment.reveal: He reached the place where the sun goes down. When he fell, his staff grew into a grove of peach trees.

misconceptions: If you can't catch it, don't chase it

quiz.question: What was Kuafu chasing?
quiz.explanation: He meant to catch the sun that rose and set each day.

quiz.question: What did his staff become after he fell?
quiz.explanation: The staff he cast aside became a grove of peach trees.

quiz.question: Which of these is most like Kuafu chasing the sun?
options: Practising football every day even though it is hard
quiz.explanation: Whether he catches it is one thing; whether he keeps chasing is another.
